title: Independent duration census for the RM14 dynamic-top Richards failure
question: Is the RM14 failure caused by the 8.64-second outer physical window being outside the inherited F-GC44 numerical envelope, or does the same dynamic-top state/forcing remain structurally unqualified even at much shorter independently restarted windows?

fixed_origin.initial_pressure_profile: same F-GC44 hydrostatic one-column accepted origin

method: Each census point restarts from the identical accepted F-GC44 origin.
Each point uses the same 36 cm/day dynamic-top irrigation rate; only the independently requested diagnostic interval is shorter.
The production transaction policy is not modified inside a census point.
Record status, accepted_substeps, attempts, solver_rejections, temporal_rejections, temporal_unavailable_rejections, mass_rejections and max_temporal_indicator.
Do not use the first successful window to retroactively change RM14 or RM13B.
decision_rules: If at least one shorter window succeeds with one or more accepted substeps, classify the RM14 failure as a bounded irrigation-aware physical-window/numerical-policy mismatch and derive a new prospective scheduler/application-window authority.

If no census point succeeds, classify the failure as structural with respect to the tested dynamic-top origin/solver/certificate route and investigate solver/certificate construction before any new triangle attempt.
Mass rejection at any point is a separate accounting blocker and must not be conflated with solver or temporal failure.
nonclaims: RM15 is diagnostic only and does not admit a smaller irrigation timestep for production.
The total delivered depth differs across diagnostic windows because the physical rate is held fixed; RM15 therefore does not replace the RM14 physical experiment.
No retry count, tolerance or temporal budget is tuned.
No MODFLOW or Ribasim execution is needed in RM15.
